formula_checks.name: equityByMonth
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Allocates a level annual run-rate using all vest months and ignores which calendar year actually vests. It silently puts undated vesting in December.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Read year-specific vested values for actual months, or clearly label an illustrative run-rate.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: equityByMonth reads only the MONTH of each vest date and spreads the level run-rate rsuAnnual (total / number of vest years) over those months. buildDatedGrid lays this on real dated months: vests Mar 2026 $8,317.43, Jun 2027 $1,321.19, Dec 2027 $4,211.17 give Equity vesting Dec 2026 $2,105.585, Mar 2027 $4,158.715, Jun 2027 $660.595 on the Oct 2026–Sep 2027 table, where only Jun 2027 $1,321.19 vests. An undated vest goes to December (case C05, NEEDS RULING).

formula_checks.name: daysBetweenDates
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Elapsed milliseconds rounded to days does not define calendar-day behavior across daylight saving time and non-midnight timestamps.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Declare whole local calendar dates versus elapsed 24-hour periods; normalize the former before subtraction.
formula_checks.fix_kind: app fix + records fix (rule text: calendar days)
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: round(elapsed milliseconds / 86,400,000). Its caller compares a bill's local midnight with the clock time now: a bill due today is listed until noon (round(-0.46) = -0) and dropped after noon (round(-0.54) = -1). DST alone is harmless for midnight dates.
formula_checks.plain_example: Bill due Dec 15, opened Dec 15 at 11:00: listed, 0 days away; at 13:00: gone.

formula_checks.name: nextOccurrence
formula_checks.reviewer_why: The revised rule deliberately leaves earlier days in the current month in the past, despite a purpose that says next occurrence on/after now. Leap-day rollover is also unspecified.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Name it current-cycle occurrence or implement true next occurrence; settle February 29 in nonleap years. Preserve the owner’s current-month bill rule at its caller.
formula_checks.fix_kind: app fix + records fix (rule text: "this cycle's date", per DEC-7941)
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: The current-month rule follows DEC-7941 (case C05 agrees). But new Date(year, month - 1, day) rolls a day past the month's end into the next month: Feb 29 in 2027 is listed 2027-03-01 and a September 31 bill 2027-10-01, while the month table counts both in their own month. The editor's day field is free text (2 digits).
formula_checks.plain_example: $300 fee, February, day 29: list says due Mar 1 2027; the table has it in February 2027. Right: the month's last day (Feb 28).

formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-BILLS): a day past its month's end is the month's last day — Feb 29 is 2027-02-28, on the list and the table alike.

formula_checks.name: upcomingBills
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Undated annual categories are spread over twelve months by the budget reader but placed wholly in January here. The relationship to conservative availability is clear, but bill timing/unknown coverage is inconsistent.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Use one dated bill schedule or flag unentered due months; keep same-day bill allocation stable and avoid inventing January.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: A once-in-a-while category with no month is listed as due 1 January at its full amount (ms = [1]), while the budget spreads it at a twelfth a month. The month table it reads (buildDatedGrid, same [1] default) then counts it twice when the bill is bigger than the month's plan: $1,200 in January + $100 in each of 11 other months = $2,300 a year (P2). With $2,000 typed a month the year holds ($24,000) but January shows $800 everyday + $1,200 bill (P3). The dated example ($2,000 + $1,200 December) is right everywhere: Sep $2,000, Dec $3,200, year $25,200, one $1,200 bill on Dec 15 (P1). The same-day tie is stable (C03 agrees).
formula_checks.plain_example: Only budget line: $1,200 insurance, no month. Budget $100 a month ($1,200 a year); bill list "$1,200 due Jan 1 2027"; month table $2,300 for the year.

The precision guard's rounding pattern looks only for x 100 / 1e4 / 10000, so it does not see x 1000. A limit of 0 or less refuses (null), right.
